evidence.source: 《说文解字》 text and Duan Yucai commentary, accessed through 汉典
evidence.field: 了字说文解字 / 说文解字注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry says 尦也。从子無臂。象形 (“crossed legs; from 子 without arms; pictographic”). Duan Yucai glosses 尦 as legs crossing while walking and describes 了戾 as things twisted or knotted rather than straight; he says the character was borrowed for 憭悟, ‘understand/clear’. This is an historical analysis, not independent proof of the depicted referent.
evidence.title: 了 liǎo、le - 汉典

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese glyph origin and etymology sections
evidence.text: The page reports a Shuowen pictographic interpretation as a baby without arms and cites a commentary interpretation of entangled legs. It says the relation of ‘finish’ to the graph may be a phonetic loan, while ‘entangled legs → tie → finish’ is another proposed semantic path. It reports verb ‘finish/be completed’ developing into perfective 了 and subsequently a sentence-final change-of-state particle, with the perfective use common by Tang. The page says ancient-form data mainly derives from Richard Sears’ Chinese Etymology collections; no primary ancient inscription image was inspected here, so an original referent or paleographic sequence cannot be confirmed from this evidence.
evidence.title: 了 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Min-a Park, article abstract indexed by Korea Citation Index
evidence.text: The study summarizes Tang–Song uses in V-le, V-O-le, and V-le-O sequences: it analyzes early 了 as a verb ‘finish’, then as a resultative complement, and reports Song examples of V-le-O marking perfective aspect. It also reports post-Song V-O-le before sentence-final 也 as an anterior marker. This provides a scholarly account of layered developments; the abstract does not supply dated primary quotations, so exact earliest attestations remain unverified here.
evidence.title: On Grammatical Functions and Meanings of the Verb ‘–Le’ in the Tang-Song Dynasties

evidence.text: The page quotes older lexicographic senses including 慧也，曉解也 (‘intelligent; understand clearly’) and 訖也，畢也 (‘finished; completed’), with citations to Han-period biography, Song history, Jin history, and Tang Du Fu. These are citations reported by a later dictionary and do not establish which sense came first. Example: Du Fu’s Tang poem has 未了, ‘not ended/finished’.

evidence.text: Unicode documents character lookup by hexadecimal code point and describes Unihan as a database of properties including kMandarin. The required direct character-specific records could not be opened through the browser. Local checkout contains only pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv and has no row for either 了 or 瞭; sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt and sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv are absent. Thus no local reading rows or Baxter–Sagart comparison can be reported.

evidence.text: A nonofficial Unihan mirror displays kMandarin le, kDefinition ‘to finish; particle of completed action’, kTang *leǔ leǔ, and simplified/traditional variant links to 瞭. This is useful only as a secondary transcription; it does not substitute for the required inspected official Unicode character record. The official endpoint was attempted and inaccessible.

evidence.source: Unicode Character database mirror; Unicode official per-codepoint endpoint was inaccessible
evidence.text: A nonofficial Unihan mirror displays kMandarin liào liǎo, kDefinition ‘bright, clear; clear-sighted’, kTang leu lěu, and identifies 了 as a simplified variant of 瞭. A Unicode proposal result independently shows the proposed kMandarin values liào liǎo and notes simplification of 瞭 to 了 except for liào readings. Official per-codepoint lookup for U+77AD could not be opened.
evidence.title: U+77AD ‘瞭’ CJK Unified Ideograph

evidence.source: Unicode Consortium, proposal to change kMandarin values
evidence.text: A Unicode proposal lists 瞭’s then-current kMandarin as liǎo and proposed values liào liǎo, explaining that 瞭 is simplified to 了 except when read liào. This supports the distinction of readings and variant scope, but is proposal documentation rather than the current official character record.
evidence.title: L2/19-362: Proposal to change some kMandarin values

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced Shuowen corpus and character lookup. Character lookup result reports the seal-script Shuowen entry; direct opening of the dictionary lookup failed.
Search surfaced ancient-form categories and a modern pictogram account; no opened primary paleographic record established earliest attestation or referent.

Search surfaced a secondary mirror and Unicode proposal documenting liào/liǎo and the simplified-variant rule.

gaps: No exact, securely dated earliest attestation for the graph or for the lexical verb meaning ‘finish’ was established in the inspected sources. The Shuowen account is received historical testimony, not direct confirmation of the pictorial referent.

The competing interpretations—child without arms, crossed lower legs, or entangled legs—remain analyses of the graph; no visually inspected oracle-bone, bronze, or seal exemplar was available to adjudicate them.

The proposed ‘entangled/tangled → tied → finished’ semantic bridge is not demonstrated by dated intermediate usages. Sound-loan explanation is asserted by a secondary account, but an early source spelling and phonological basis were not independently verified.

The Tang/Song grammaticalization sequence is supported by a scholarly abstract and a secondary synthesis, but no dated primary quotations were inspected. The proposal that final 了 may coalesce with 也 in some dialects remains tentative.

No tool inspection verified the required official Unicode character-specific pages despite attempts. Secondary mirrors report current readings 了 le and 瞭 liào/liǎo. The local HSK extract contains neither row; the full Unihan readings and Baxter–Sagart datasets are absent from this checkout.

No phonetic-component analysis applies to 子 under the received Shuowen account; the dossier’s baby/swaddling gloss is mnemonic-like and not independently established. 了 is reported as a phonetic component in compounds elsewhere, but that is distinct from the formation of 了 itself.
No bulk source extract is recommended: the consulted pages are character-specific or have unclear reuse terms; no permission for a local corpus extract was verified.
